To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the desorption of PAHs from soil into aqueoues phase can be enhanced by the co-existence Tween 80 and the DOM derived from pig compost or pig manure.

the coexistence between Tween 80 and the dissolved organic matter (derived from pig manure and pig manure compost) in soil-water system could enhance the desorption and the subsequent bioavailability of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).
the coexistence effect of nonionic micellar surfactant and DOM on the desorption of PAHs was more than the individual effect of each of them in soil-water system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the combined effect of nonionic Tween 80 and natural organic matter on the desorption behaviors of phenanthrene, pyrene, and other HOCs in soil environment.
the combined effect of nonionic Tween 80 surfactant and DOM derived from different sources on the desorption of HOCs in the soil-water environment.
the combined effect of nonionic Tween 80 and natural DOM derived from pig compost or pig manure on the behaviors of HOCs in soil-water system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of both DOM and nonionic surfactants in soil environment could enhance the desorption and bioavailability of HOCs, which is of great importance to the remediation and management of HOCs-contaminated soil.
the coexistence or co-exposure of DOM and surfactant in the soil environment may enhance the bioavailability or desorption of HOCs.
the co-existence effect of DOM and Tween 80 is a possible explanation of the desorption phenomenon of PAHs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both Tween 80 alone and Tween 80 with coexistence of DOM derived from pig compost and pig manur could significantly enhance the desorption behavior and bioavailability of PAHS in soil-water system.
the co-existence and the interaction of DOM and nonionic surfactants in the soil-water environment could enhance the desorption and the bioavailability of HOCs.
both DOM derived from pig compost and pig manures and surfactant Tween-80 could enhance the desorption and bioavailability of HOCs in the soil-water systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the coexistence and interaction between nonionic surfactants and dissolved organic matter in soil-water system may play a significant role in enhancing the desorption of PAHs and HOCs in soil environment.
the coexistence effect of DOM and surfactants should be considered in the design of remediation strategy for soil contaminated with HOCs.
the combined effect of Tween 80 (surfactant) and DOM (natural organic matter) should be considered for remediation of PAHs contaminated soils.
